title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: two small categories A and B, with presheaf categories A^, B^ and (A×B)^. Grothendieck uses the identification (A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°, B^), X ↦ X'' with X''(a) = X(a,−).

His projection notation is consistent throughout the computation: the subscript names the factor that is forgotten. So p_B : A×B → A and p_A : A×B → B. Under this convention p_A^*(M) makes sense for M in B^, and p_B^*(a) makes sense for a in A.

Step 1 (a struck-out opening, 'a third interpretation of the functor Γ''_b'). For an object b of B, let ε_b : B^ → Ens be evaluation at b, ε_b(G) = Hom(b,G) = G(b). Then Γ''_b(X) = ε_b ∘ X''. This is the presheaf a ↦ X(a,b) on A, i.e. the restriction of X to the slice A×{b}.

Step 2 (generalisation). Replace the representable b by an arbitrary presheaf M in B^. Put ε_M(G) = Hom_{B^}(M,G) and define Γ''_M(X) = ε_M ∘ X''. Concretely, Γ''_M(X)(a) = Hom_{B^}(M, X(a,−)). In enriched-category language this is the M-weighted limit of X in the B-variable.

Step 3 (claim). Γ''_M(X) ≃ p_{B*} Hom(p_A^*(M), X), naturally in M and X. Here Hom is the internal Hom of the topos (A×B)^ and p_{B*} is direct image to A^.

Step 4 (proof by Yoneda). Fix a in A and compute both sides of Hom_{A^}(a, −).
- Left side: Γ''_M(X)(a) = Hom_{B^}(M, X''(a)). He then uses X''(a) ≃ p_{A*} Hom(p_B^*(a), X). This holds because evaluating at b gives Hom(p_B^*a × p_A^*b, X) = X(a,b), since p_B^*a × p_A^*b is the representable (a,b). By the adjunction p_A^* ⊣ p_{A*} and currying, the left side becomes Hom(p_A^*M, Hom(p_B^*a, X)) = Hom(p_A^*M × p_B^*a, X).
- Right side: by the adjunction p_B^* ⊣ p_{B*}, it is Hom(p_B^*a, Hom(p_A^*M, X)) = Hom(p_B^*a × p_A^*M, X).

The two sides agree ('OK!'). Equivalently, Γ''_M is right adjoint to the external product A^ → (A×B)^, F ↦ F ⊠ M.

Purpose: in these 'closed models' notes (paper reused from a June 1982 printout), this is a technical lemma giving a formula for 'section/restriction' functors Γ'' on bi-presheaves. Such functors are used when comparing homotopy theories of presheaves on product categories, as in the test-category and integrator discussions of Pursuing Stacks.
errors: The line defining Γ''_M reads 'X'' ↦ ε_M ∘ Γ''_M'; it should read ε_M ∘ X''. This is a slip.
In the left column, the line 'p_{A*}(Hom(p_B^*(a), X))' is missing the outer Hom_{B^}(M, −). It should be Hom_{B^}(M, p_{A*} Hom(p_B^*(a), X)). The next step uses it correctly.
The projection notation (p_B : A×B → A, p_A : A×B → B) is the opposite of the usual convention. It is used consistently, so this is not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Identification of presheaves on A×B with functors A° → B^ (currying)
ideas.modern_name: Cartesian closedness of Cat / exponential adjunction for presheaf categories
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exposé I (general presheaf yoga); used in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Γ''_M(X)(a) = Hom_{B^}(M, X(a,−)) ≃ p_* Hom(p'^*M, X), i.e. the right adjoint of the external product F ↦ F ⊠ M, proved via Yoneda and the adjunctions p^* ⊣ p_*
ideas.modern_name: weighted limit / end formula; right adjoint to external tensor product of presheaves
ideas.where_published: similar manipulations occur in Pursuing Stacks (sections on integrators/asphericity of products), exact location unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but routine Yoneda/adjunction verification of a standard formula for bi-presheaves (a weighted limit as direct image of an internal Hom). It contains nothing a specialist would find new. The only mildly interesting point is historical: the paper is reused from a printout dated 4 June 1982. That is consistent with the notes being written from mid-1982, possibly before Pursuing Stacks (begun February 1983) rather than after it, as the archive label tentatively suggests.
transcription_corrections: The definition line should be read as 'Γ''_M : X'' ↦ ε_M ∘ X''' in intent; the image literally shows 'ε_M ∘ Γ''_M', which is Grothendieck's slip.
In the struck-out formula at the top, the first argument is p_A^*(b) and the inner Hom is underlined (internal Hom). It is only partially legible.
'Γ''_b(X')(a) = ε_b∘X'': the '(a)' is struck through in the image.
'fonct. en M, X, a' is written in the right margin, abbreviated as 'f— en M, X, a'.
The left column after 'Hom(M, X''(a))' carries a subscript B^ under Hom (Hom_{B^}).
